children: Travelers reported higher quarterly profit, despite roughly flat revenue, helped by investment gains.
The insurance company on Friday posted a third-quarter profit of $1.92 billion, or $9.04 a share, compared with $1.89 billion, or $8.24 a share, a year earlier.
Core earnings per share were $9.18, compared with analyst estimates of $7.39, according to FactSet.
Profit was boosted by the company's investment portfolio--with net investment income up 6% to a record $1.1 billion pre-tax--but was dented by higher catastrophe losses.
Revenue was roughly flat at $12.41 billion, topping analyst estimates of $11.36 billion. Net written premiums were also roughly flat from a year ago at $11.48 billion.
Chief Executive Alan Schnitzer pointed to strong underwriting performance across all of Travelers' three segments, and said the company is well-positioned to finish the year strong.
"That momentum, and the advances we are making on our innovation agenda, give us real confidence heading into 2027 and beyond," he said.
